observations.evidence: Rounded containers separate panels (a)–(c), each with a left input, central denoising arrow, and stacked right outputs. Enlarged sign regions support close comparison.
observations.limitation: The two prompts in panel (b) require extra effort to associate with their respective outputs.

observations.limitation: Panel (b)'s multiline prompt and vertically separated conditions require extra effort to associate with their outputs.

source.caption:
Figure 2. The overview of Entropy-based Uncertainty Modeling and Self-training framework. 1) The model is first trained on the labeled
base set. 2) For the novel images, the saliency maps are generated from a saliency model and high confidence base pixels are ignored. We
then apply clustering to the novel salient part to obtain clustering pseudo-labels. 3) We apply entropy ranking and dynamic reassignment
to split clean and unclean novel images and utilize them to optimize the model with clustering labels and online labels, respectively.

observations.evidence: The three stages show supervised segmentation, saliency-assisted clustering, and training with clean and unclean pseudo-labels.
observations.limitation: The transition from Stage Two into entropy ranking is not explicitly connected, and repeated network icons lack role labels.

observations.evidence: Three stages show base-image supervision, saliency-guided clustering, and training with clean and unclean images. Example masks make removal of base-class pixels understandable.

source.caption:
Figure 1: From stateless refinement to continual capability growth. VEvo-Harness causally verifies
and reuses visual experience, enabling frozen generators to become progressively stronger with usage.

observations.evidence: The discarded results on the left contrast explicitly with memory and reusable skills in the center. The rising versus plateauing curves reinforce the motivation for accumulating experience.
observations.limitation: The repeated example images do not clearly identify which failures are repaired or which capabilities improve.

observations.evidence: The left workflow ends in discarded repair experience, while the central loop retains experience as reusable skills. The right growth curves reinforce the contrast between stateless refinement and accumulated capability.
observations.limitation: The surrounding example imagery and multiple benefit claims compete with the central motivational contrast.

observations.evidence: The left workflow explicitly discards repair experience, while the central memory-to-skills pathway retains it. The right-side growth chart reinforces the contrast between stateless repetition and accumulated capability.
observations.limitation: The smaller supporting mechanisms require closer inspection than the main contrast.

observations.evidence: The left workflow, central learning loop, and right benefits form recognizable groups. Crops make most explanatory labels readable.
observations.limitation: The oversized title, illustrated background, bottom timeline, and social post compete with the central comparison for attention.

observations.evidence: Three major regions separate the baseline, proposed approach, and benefits; the baseline has a clear downward sequence. Component cards group the central loop into named operations.
observations.limitation: Dense annotations, a large illustrated header, the bottom episode sequence, and the social-post example create several competing reading paths.

source.title: Learning to Restore More: Continual Capability Expansion for Pretrained Image Restoration Models
source.role_reason: 3.2节与图2明确给出整体框架，含冻结复原骨干、残差扩展模块、两级路由与专家库的完整计算路径。

source.caption:
Figure 2: Overview of the proposed RestoreMore framework. A pretrained restoration model is
preserved as a frozen capability anchor, and lightweight residual expansion modules are inserted at
selected feature stages. Inside each expansion module, a degradation descriptor is first constructed
from spatial and frequency statistics. Top-M capability selection is then performed over accumu-
lated capability prototypes and routers. The selected routers further retrieve complementary experts
from the expert-key bank through query–key matching. Frozen historical components and trainable
current-task components are indicated by snowflake and flame icons, respectively.

source.title: Sprout: Building Dynamic Memory While Reasoning for Agentic Video Understanding
source.role_reason: 引言图1对比离线构建静态记忆与推理时动态构建，解释旧方案无法更新与成本问题；保留同图性能面板。
source.caption:
Figure 1: (a) Offline memory is first built for the whole video before the first question; Q1–Q6 then
reason over the same memory without updating it. Nodes used by a question take that question’s
color, and the rest are never touched. (b) Per-question tokens with Gemini 3.8 Flash as the model.
Direct feeds the video and question directly to the model. Offline memory is Qwen-MM-Plugins:
its construction cost, amortized over the benchmark’s questions. Our method has no construction
stage. (c) Sprout builds memory while reasoning. The agent watches the video segment by segment
at a low frame rate and stops once the question has enough evidence, so the tail of the video is never
watched and costs nothing. Each watched segment is remembered as a coarse textual node written
into memory; revisits at a higher frame rate add child nodes beneath the intervals a question needs.

source.role_reason: 图2明确为GenerateU整体模型及两种训练策略，涵盖图像编码、检测、适配和语言生成路径。
source.caption:
Figure 2. Overview of our proposed open-ended object detection model, GenerateU, which comprises two major components: an object
detector and a language model. We compare two training strategies: (Top) We incorporate the class-agnostic DETR (with frozen image
encoder) into a pre-trained and frozen Multimodal Large Language Model (including Adaptor and Language Model), to facilitate a smooth
transfer of knowledge from the language domain to object detection; (Bottom) We activate the image encoder and language model as
trainable components, taking an end-to-end approach to seamlessly integrate region-level understanding into the language model.

source.caption:
Figure 2. Framework of our proposed Relation-aware Intra-modal Matching (RIM) Network. We first explore Stable Diffusion model and
SAM to construct image-modal reference features, then we conduct relation-aware matching between region features and reference features
based on ranking distribution. The matching is established in the all-purpose feature spaces of DINOv2.

Figure 2. Diagram of our proposed method. Offline Labeller Training: we add a detector head to a frozen DINOv2 encoder and train
it with source images only. Offline Label Generation: we combine and freeze the labeller backbone and detector, and generate target
pseudo-labels. Online Student Training: We train a student network using source ground truth boxes and target pseudo-labels, and align
patch features to a frozen DINOv2 encoder. During inference, the alignment encoder and projection MLP are not used.

source.role_reason: 引言第2页明确引用图1(c)说明闭集方法无法发现训练类别之外的物体，图注解释SS碎片和Mask R-CNN漏检；按具体开放世界失败案例收录，保留全部八个子图。
source.caption:
Figure 1. Comparison of GGN with different baselines. (a) an input image from ADE20K [61] (upper row) with the ground truth
object masks overlaid (lower row). Three different approaches: (b) Selective Search (SS) [51], (c) Mask R-CNN [22], and (d) our Generic
Grouping Network (GGN) are applied on the same image to predict the top 100 proposals. The upper images provide all top-100 proposals
predicted by three approaches with false and true positive proposals visualized in red and green boxes, respectively. The lower images
provide only true positive proposals. The number of true positive proposals or ground truth objects are denoted in parentheses. Among 20
ground truth objects, SS recalls only 4, Mask R-CNN detects 5, and GGN retrieves 14. SS is a bottom-up non-parametric approach, thus
has no notion of objectness. Mask R-CNN can make whole object proposals; however it still fails to detect objects that are not seen during
training. Our GGN can predict whole object proposals and generalize to unseen categories.

source.caption: Figure 1: Object semantics for open-ended naming and spatial prediction. (a) Spatial prediction produces object queries for LLM-based naming. (b) UniOSE enriches these queries with image-derived regional semantics and uses them for training-time detection matching and mask conditioning. Semantic guidance originates from the enriched query before LLM-based naming. (c) Comparison of box recall@0.75 and naming accuracy. Swin and SAM denote Open-Det Swin-T and its fully fine-tuned SAM2-T backbone variant, respectively. The protocol, metric definitions, and source results are provided in Appendix A.1.

source.caption:
Figure 1: We present PCAsplat, a geometric regularization of Gaussian splatting that aligns Gaus-
sians with surfaces through differentiable local PCA. Compared with current methods, PCAsplat
substantially reduces floaters (left) and produces cleaner point clouds with better surface coverage
(center). This improved point-cloud enables downstream tasks such as instance segmentation (right).

observations.limitation: The room comparison lacks an explanation of what its colors represent and how it connects to surface alignment.

source.caption:
Figure 4. (a) Illustrates the training stage of the GenDeg model where it is trained to condition on the clean image, text prompt and mean
intensity (µ) and variation (σ) of the degradation pattern. (b) Shows the inference stage where the model generates a degraded image based
on these conditions; and (c) Depicts the architecture of the Swin-transformer-based restoration network.

source.caption:
Figure 1: POISE overview. The support set is encoded by a frozen DINOv2 encoder into a raw memory
bank and per-class prototype maps. TPR retrieves an adjacency set of hard negatives, renews each prototype
by a bounded one-step update, and writes the refined prototype back. UPN proposals are scored by cosine
classification against the refined prototypes; suspect screening flags nested same-class pairs and passes only
those to OAD, which separates whole objects from fragments.

dual-branch inference. At time step t, the main branch predicts depth and pose from
state s using both image and RayMap features. The predicted pose Tˆ is remapped
t−1 t
into RayMap and encoded into tokens r′ , then queried against the frozen state s
t t−1
by the RayMap branch to obtain a static-biased prediction. The depth difference
between branches is pro jected via image-state attention to form staticness weights α
t
that suppress dynamic regions during state update (s = s + α ⊙ ∆s ). This dual-
t t−1 t t
branch scheme identifies and suppresses dynamic regions at inference time.

source.caption:
Figure 1. NAS3R is a self-supervised framework that requires no ground-truth annotations and no pretrained priors during training, and
jointly infers 3D Gassian parameters, camera intrinsics and extrinsics and depth maps, also enabling high-quality novel view synthesis.

observations.limitation: The small colored camera-like objects do not separately explain camera and depth outputs.

observations.limitation: The camera and depth-map symbols are not individually explained.

observations.limitation: The individual depth and camera outputs are less explicitly distinguished within the reconstruction.

source.caption:
Figure 2: OpenAgentFlow normalizes instrumented actions into AgentEvents and checks them
with a shared PEP before execution; the control plane maintains policy, provenance, session, audit,
and update state.

observations.evidence: The main pipeline runs visibly from agents through adapters and event normalization to policy enforcement and executors. Control and action planes distinguish management from execution.

source.title: CADForge: Agentic Single-View CAD Reconstruction with Explicit Geometry Reasoning
source.role_reason: 图1和方法节描述从单图分解、几何观察、编程、验证到工具自构建的整体路径。
source.caption:
Figure 1: Overview of CADForge. Given a single image, CADForge decomposes the object into
several components and constructs them progressively. For each component, geometry observation
identifies reference components and CAD-relevant constraints, while geometry programming trans-
lates them into key modeling parameters. A code generator then synthesizes executable CadQuery
code, and a review agent evaluates the result and provides targeted feedback. Throughout the pro-
cess, a compact parametric CAD memory maintains essential CAD state for on-demand retrieval,
while a failure-guided toolkit offers reusable helpers for robust code generation.

source.title: TIR-Agent: Training an Explorative and Efficient Agent for Image Restoration
source.role_reason: 引言图1比较整合模型、无需训练的智能体与可训练智能体，明确标注次优任务规划和冗余调用问题。
source.caption:
Fig.1: Comparison of restoration paradigms. (a) All-in-one model: Uses
a single network with specialized heads to inject various degradation features. (b)
Training-free Agent: Uses VLMs for static task planning, executing sub-tasks se-
quentially via exhaustive tool traversal. (c) TIR-Agent (Ours): A trainable agent
that dynamically decides the next sub-task based on current results and learns to di-
rectly select the optimal tool, avoiding redundant execution.

observations.evidence: The three panels contrast an all-in-one model, a fixed-plan agent with rollback, and an adaptive agent that changes dehazing to brightening. Red inefficiency labels and green efficiency labels make the intended motivation explicit.
observations.limitation: The limitation of the all-in-one model is less explicitly communicated than the fixed-plan agent's limitation.

source.caption:
Figure 3. Qualitative comparison against deterministic monocular 3D human reconstruction methods [5, 10] that predict geometry,
surface albedo and shaded colour. PHORHUM [5] (retrained on our dataset) outputs good front predictions, but exhibits over-smooth, flat
geometry and blurry colours on the back. S3F [10] yields more detailed geometry, but colours are still often blurry. Moreover, both these
methods occasionally paste the front colour predictions onto the back incorrectly (see row 3). Our method outputs multiple diverse samples,
with a greater level of geometric detail and colour sharpness in uncertain regions, that are consistent with the input image after shading.

producesaFine-grainedPerceptualDegradationMapthatcapturesspatiallylocalizeddefectlikelihoodandintensity, andtherewardmodel

source.title: Frozen CLIP: A Strong Backbone for Weakly Supervised Semantic Segmentation
source.role_reason: 图2及3.1节明确为完整WeCLIP，涵盖冻结骨干、分类CAM、分割解码及精炼模块。
source.caption:
Figure 2. Framework of our WeCLIP. The image is input to the Frozen CLIP image encoder to generate the image features, and class
labels are used to build text prompts and then input to the Frozen CLIP text encoder to generate the text features. The classification scores
are generated based on the distance between the pooled image and text features. Using GradCAM, we can generate the initial CAM
M . Then, the frozen image features from the last layer of each transformer block are input to our decoder to generate the final semantic
init
segmentation predictions. Meanwhile, the affinity map A from our decoder and the multi-head attention maps A from CLIP are input to
f s
our RFM to establish refining maps R to refine M as M . After post-processing, it will be used as the supervision to train our decoder.
init f

observations.evidence: The image and prompt inputs lead visibly through CLIP encoders, a decoder, and prediction/pseudo-label supervision. Heatmaps show the transition from initial activation to refined localization.

source.caption: Figure 3. Overview of the training pipeline. Our framework operates in two stages. Base Training (blue and green) establishes independent student-teacher setups for each modality using sparse supervision. Cross-Modal Consistency (orange) introduces our core contribution: bidirectional knowledge transfer where the teacher of one modality supervises the student of the other, weighted by our dual confidence mechanism leveraging prediction certainty and reconstruction quality.

Figure 1: Overview of OmniClinic. Each electronic health record instantiates a patient agent and
defines the case evidence. The sandbox exposes a finite action space spanning clinical consultation
and bedside physical examinations with common clinical tools. The doctor agent selects among these
actions to acquire multimodal evidence before submitting a diagnosis. Examination succeeds only
with the appropriate tool, body region, patient pose, and doctor (agent) position.

source.caption:
Figure 3: Overview of Classwise State Routing. Top: A labeled calibration set estimates down-
stream class-by-state reliability, selects a compact shared state pool, and fixes class-conditioned
routing weights. Bottom: For a new image, the frozen backbone extracts selected-state responses,
which are fused and rescaled before unchanged backend-native decoding.

observations.evidence: The two stages show labeled calibration data producing reliability estimates and image responses undergoing weighted fusion to segmentation outputs.
observations.limitation: The transfer of selected states and learned weights from calibration into fusion is implied rather than explicitly connected.

Figure 2. Overview of our proposed framework GenNBV. Our end-to-end policy takes the historical multi-source observations as input,
transforms them into a more informative scene representation, and produces the next viewpoint position. A reward signal will be returned
at training time to optimize the end-to-end policy for maximizing the expected cumulative reward in one episode. Specifically, the signal
is the increased coverage ratio after collecting a new viewpoint.

source.caption:
Figure 1. The main idea promoted throughout the paper is that
semantic context prototype-aware underpins localization of indi-
vidual objects in WSSS. Our CPAL performs adaptive perception
of diverse attributes (e.g., cat) with attribute hunting (c) rather
than from single prototype (a) and plain context prototypes (b).
This attribute-specific adaptation not only mitigates the risk of er-
rors where (b) mistakenly identifies similar categories (e.g., dog)
but also ensures accurate activation of the complete object region.

source.title: Learning Affinity from Attention: End-to-End Weakly-Supervised Semantic Segmentation with Transformers
source.role_reason: 图3明确为端到端WSSS整体框架，包含编码、CAM、AFA、随机游走、PAR和分割监督路径。
source.caption:
Figure 3. The proposed end-to-end framework for WSSS. We use a Transformer backbone as the encoder to extract feature maps. The
initial pseudo labels are generated with CAM [59] and then refined with the proposed PAR. In the AFA module, we derive the semantic
affinity from MHSA in Transformer blocks. AFA is supervised with the pseudo affinity labels derived from the refined label. Next, we
employ the learned affinity to revise the pseudo labels via random walk propagation [2, 1]. The propagated labels are finally refined with
PAR as the pseudo labels for the segmentation branch.

source.caption:
Figure 1. To determine the best view for 3D reconstruction, previous methods only chose from hand-crafted action space or based on
object-centric capturing, lacking the ability to generalize to unforeseen scenes (Left). With our end-to-end trained, generalized free-space
policy, it can generalize to unseen objects, enabling the captured drone to image from any viewpoint (Right).

source.caption:
Figure 3: Overview of InstaPoint. IDC initializes instance-wise assignments to SAM or watershed
using class-calibrated point spacing. ISA then makes a one-time selection of the source with the
lower GWD-based size loss relative to the detector’s current prediction.

observations.evidence: The input views, backbone, detection head, predictions, and losses form a traceable pipeline. The IDC-to-ISA transition and candidate comparison explain the assignment strategy.
observations.limitation: The exact relationship between assignment output and mask loss is less explicit than the detection path.

observations.evidence: The upper pipeline connects image views, backbone, detection head, predictions, and losses. The assignment branch explicitly shows IDC switching to ISA after T epochs.
observations.limitation: How the selected supervision feeds the mask loss is less explicit than the detector pathway.

observations.evidence: The upper pipeline connects image views, backbone, detection head, predictions, and losses. Expanded IDC and ISA panels explain density-based candidate selection and prediction-based comparison.
observations.limitation: How the original and augmented views contribute separately to the training paths remains implicit.

observations.limitation: Tracing the prediction feedback connector through the mask-loss path requires extra attention.

source.caption:
Figure 2: Overview of PAIR3D. PAIR3D aligns reconstructed 3D scenes with physical constraints
through verifiable feedback. Given an initial SAM3D reconstruction with artifacts such as floating
objects and inter-object penetration, we construct a multimodal relational scene graph from object
states, spatial visual evidence, and pairwise relations. A shared relational encoder provides structure-
aware representations to an actor–critic policy, which iteratively updates object translation, rotation,
and scale. Physics simulation and visual verification provide verifiable rewards for PPO training. The
resulting policy directly refines scenes at test time, reducing penetration and support violations while
producing configurations that remain stable under simulation.

source.title: Maestro: Agentic Formal Proof Development by Coordination
source.role_reason: 图1和正文展示协调者、并行证明工作者、事件队列、共享工作区与最终检查的循环。
source.caption:
Figure 1: MAESTRO’s coordination loop. The persistent coordinator 1 dispatches or redirects
workers, which 2 attack open obligations in parallel and 3 report proofs, diagnoses, progress, or
blueprints to a shared queue. The coordinator 4 consumes these events as they arrive and 5 revises
the shared Lean workspace, here retracting H2 and H1.2, restating H3 as H3’, adding H4, and
keeping the proved H1.1. When the root closes, 6 Lean checks the final proof or falsification.

source.role_reason: 图1显示既有质量指标偏好失真输出而非感知更自然的重建，正文据此引出LR条件奖励与人类偏好的对齐问题。
source.caption:
Fig. 1: Overview of our proposed evaluation paradigm. (a) HR A preserves structures,
while HR B shows severe distortions. (b) RefReward-SR uses an MLLM for inter-
pretable, LR-conditioned semantic scoring. (c) Existing metrics wrongly favor the dis-
torted HR B, whereas ours aligns with human perception. (d) RefReward-SR uniquely
ensures semantic fidelity and preference alignment without GT dependency. The as-
terisk(*) indicates that FR metrics evaluate high-level semantics only passively via
low-level correspondence.

try tokens with a DINOv2 backbone, then decouples them into scene geometry and motion geometry
tokens. The scene decoder predicts camera parameters and depth, while the motion decoder esti-
mates sparse se(3) transforms and motion base weights for dense SE(3) projection.

Figure 1. Motivation for FinPercep-RM and CCL. (a) Standard
IQAs lack fine-grained perception and struggle to penalize lo-
cal distortions, while Ours aligns with human judgment (User
Study). (b) The training curves illustrate the stability-robustness
dilemma: baseline IQA rewards (blue/purple) converge quickly,
while FinPercep-RM (light blue) is oscillatory and unstable. Our
completemethod(FinPercep-RMw/CCL,orange)achievesstable
and optimal convergence. (c) Visualization of Reward Hacking:
baseline rewards (W/ CLIP-IQA, W/ MAN-IQA) produce local
artifacts, whereas our results are faithful to the Ground Truth.

source.caption:
Figure 2: SAM challenges. Left: As an instance-based model, SAM performs poorly when segmenting a
class comprising multiple instances, see the class “person”. Splitting the class mask into individual instances
addresses this challenge. Middle: Confidence-based sampling (Kweon & Yoon, 2024) yields a suboptimal
mask; in contrast, our proposed sampling strategy achieves comprehensive mask coverage, resulting in im-
proved segmentation. Right: SAM score-based mask selection may not give the best desired segmentation
(see mask in red box). Our mask selection strategy using intersection with the coarse mask determines the
desired mask granularity (see mask in green box).

source.caption:
Figure 2. The training process of SPG: each style reference guides the source image through a dedicated generator G to produce a style-
i
aware prompt. Prompts are merged and used to optimize a frozen privacy model. Each style-prompt generator consists of a modulation
network and a learnable prompt template, producing the final style-prompt via element-wise modulation.

Figure 1. Conceptual illustration. (a) Without priors, grounding
detectors trained with limited labels often ignore spatial/semantic
cues (e.g., “on the left”). (b) HeROD injects heuristic-inspired
reasoning priors (spatial + semantic), guiding the detector toward
correct localization and improving data-efficient learning.

source.caption:
Figure 1: Motivation of DCHA. (a) Existing category-level methods rigidly assign fixed experts
based on category, whereas DCHA dynamically selects and composes fine-grained parameter vec-
tors according to category demands. (b) Category-specific updates produced by existing category-
level methods exhibit uniformly high pairwise similarities within the same task. (c) Shared bank
parameter deviations progressively accumulate at the vector, category, and task levels during incre-
mental training, resulting in hierarchical drift.

source.caption:
Figure 3: The diagram of the proposed progressive end-to-end object detection framework. First, the prediction selector
select queries associated with high confidence scores as accepted queries, leaving the rest as noisy queries. Then Relation
information extractor models the relations between noisy queries and their neighbors from accepted predictions. Next, the
queries are fed into the queries updater to be further refined by performing a new local self-attention.

Figure 1. Pipeline. First, we train a UDF prediction network U on a synthetic dataset, which contains a series of local point cloud patches
Θ
that are independent of specific shapes. Given a global point cloud P, we then extract a local patch P assigned to each query point q within

Θˆ
by incorporating the DCUDF [18] framework.

source.title: Adversarial Diffusion Compression for Real-World Image Super-Resolution
source.role_reason: 引言和图1对比完整扩散模型与压缩模型的计算路径，指出冗余模块带来的高计算开销，为ADC设计引出问题。
source.caption:
Figure 1. Comparison between our proposed AdcSR and typ-
ical one-step diffusion-based Real-ISR methods. (a) The state-
of-the-art one-step diffusion network OSEDiff [96] employs com-
plete SD [80] models for Real-ISR, suffering from high computa-
tional costs. (b) We distill OSEDiff (ADC-teacher) into a smaller
diffusion-GAN hybrid model, AdcSR (ADC-student), under the
proposed ADC framework, achieving significantly improved effi-
ciency while maintaining competitive recovery performance.

source.title: Open-World Instance Segmentation: Exploiting Pseudo Ground Truth From Learned Pairwise Affinity
source.role_reason: 图2及第2页正文列出亲和预测训练、分组生成伪真值、训练通用实例提议网络三阶段，是端到端方法流程。
source.caption:
Figure 2. Overview of our approach. (a) First, a Pairwise-Affinity Predictor (PA Pred.) is trained to predict pairwise affinities using non-
exhaustive segmentation masks as supervision. (b) Once trained, PA Pred. is used to predict pairwise affinities of the images. A grouping
module is then applied on the predicted pairwise affinity maps to generate pseudo-ground-truth masks. (c) A class-agnostic generic object
proposal network (e.g., class-agnostic Mask R-CNN) is trained end-to-end using a combination of GT and generated pseudo-GT masks.

source.caption:
Figure 1: Physics alignment and visual consistency under various methods for a reconstructed
scene. We compare SAM3D (Chen et al., 2026), REST3D (Ma et al., 2026), and PAIR3D (ours)
at initialization and after 2 seconds of MuJoCo simulation, rendered from the input camera. In
this example, PAIR3D achieves the highest scene mIoU, near-zero support error, and the smallest
simulation-induced displacement, while using fewer simulation rollouts for scene refinement. The
mIoU and support error are measured at initialization; displacement denotes the maximum per-object
translation between 0 and 2 seconds.

source.caption:
Figure 4. Overview of the proposed GKD framework. GKD comprises two major parts: domain-general distillation and task learning. In
the domain-general distillation stage, the student sequentially performs task-agnostic and domain-agnostic distillation, both via the Query-
based Soft Distillation mechanism. In the task learning stage, only the decoder is trained on source annotations, while the student encoder
is frozen to preserve the domain-general representations.

source.caption:
Figure 3. Illustration of localization distillation (LD) for an edge e ∈ B = {t, b, l, r}. Only the localization branch is visualized here.
S (·, τ ) is the generalized SoftMax function with temperature τ . For a given detector, we first switch the bounding box representation
to probability distribution. Then, we determine where to distill via region weighting on the main distillation region and the valuable
localization region. Finally, we calculate the LD loss between two probability distributions predicted by the teacher and the student.

source.caption:
Figure1. Comparisonbetweendepth-based3Dreconstruction
methods and the proposed method. In depth-based methods,
key-frame depths are estimated separately from each key frame,
and later fused into a TSDF volume. In the proposed method, the
TSDF volume is directly predicted with all the key frames in a
local window. This design leads to a much more coherent recon-
struction and real-time speed.

source.title: Topologically-Aware Deformation Fields for Single-View 3D Reconstruction
source.role_reason: 图注Overview及第2页方法说明明确给出从图像、射线行进、拓扑感知变形到规范SDF生成器的完整TARS计算路径。
source.caption:
Figure 2. Overview of TARS: Given a single image, we first map a 3D point in object space to a higher-dimensional canonical space using
our learned topologically-aware deformation field. The canonical point is then mapped to its SDF value using the Canonical Shape Generator
module. We leverage an LSTM-based differentiable renderer to guide the learning of deformation and signed distance fields.

Figure 2. Qualitative analysis of receptive field patterns and segmentation performance for small-sized models (27M-29M parameters).
Left: Visualization of effective receptive fields (ERF) on the Cityscapes validation set at 1024×1024 resolution, illustrating SegMAN’s
stronger global context modeling capacity in comparison to existing state-of-the-art models. Right: Segmentation maps highlighting
SegMAN’s superior capacity to encode fine-grained local details that are often missed by existing approaches.

source.role_reason: 图2覆盖Syn4Seg的完整核心计算路径：HDIG图像生成、APE伪标注过滤/重标、SAM边界精修；保留四个子图，不仅截单个模块。
source.caption:
Fig. 2. (a), (b) Given several novel classes and their support set, we first use HDIG to synthesize high-quality, diverse novel class images proportional to the
base class images. Guided by support images, APE refines these synthesized images to generate accurate masks through two stages: Adaptive Pseudo-label
Filtering (APF) and Adaptive Pseudo-label Relabeling (APR). Specifically, APF filters noisy regions in the initial mask M to obtain M1 ; APR relabels these
unlabeled regions to yield M2 . Finally, SAM-based Boundary Refinement (SABR) further refines the mask boundaries, yielding the final M3 . (c), (d) illustrate
the details of APF and APR.

typically inject low-quality observations and semantic prompts through latent-level conditioning,
auxiliary visual-control branches, or joint token-level multimodal conditioning. Panel (a) illustrates an
additive implementation of latent-level conditioning. GRASP organizes local visual evidence, global
image context, and agent-refined semantic prompts as distinct condition streams with complementary
functions for the SR objective.

source.title: CrossSDF: 3D Reconstruction of Thin Structures From Cross-Sections
source.role_reason: 图1及引言明确指出现有OReX/Poisson/POCO在稀疏截面上产生断裂、阶梯伪影和过平滑，局部放大框用于解释薄结构重建失败。
source.caption:
Figure 1. We propose CrossSDF, a novel approach for reconstructing a 3D signed-distance field from 2D cross-sections. The input is a
set of 2D cross-sections that sample an unobserved ground-truth geometric object by planar intersection (denoted as black lines overlayed
on the ground truth Alveolis structure on the left). CrossSDF (middle) accurately reconstructs thin structures without breakages, over-
smoothing, or cross-sectional artifacts observed in competing methods (right).

source.title: Parametric Point Cloud Completion for Polygonal Surface Reconstruction
source.role_reason: 图1及引言标出既有补全方法产生的非平面点，说明点云补全不能直接保证可恢复多边形表面的局限。
source.caption:
Figure 1. Unlike conventional point cloud completion that aims
to recover individual points (middle, non-planar points shown in
red), parametric completion recovers primitive parameters along
with corresponding inlier points. PaCo recovers planar structures
(right, each color denoting a planar primitive), directly enabling
high-quality polygonal surface reconstruction.

Figure 2: Comparison between (a) prior agentic IR pipelines (top) and (b) HarnessIR (bottom).
Prior methods sequentially apply task-specific restoration models planned by VLMs to produce the
output. HarnessIR instead uses auxiliary tools for image-specific evidence, composes a restoration
instruction for MFM, and invokes verification-driven re-execution when necessary.

source.role_reason: 第3节及图2明确展示supervision enhancement整体框架；完整保留监督增强、频率掩码生成和输出细化三个子图。
source.caption: Figure 2. Overview of our framework. (a) The supervision enhancement framework produces enhanced ground truth images by fusing frequency components from the original ground truth I_0^GT and its super-resolved variants I_i^GT using adaptive frequency masks M_i. (b) The conditional frequency mask generator constructs M_i by combining predefined masks R_b weighted with predicted coefficients c_{i,b}, followed by a softmax function. (c) The output refinement network (ORNet) is trained with this enhanced supervision to improve perceptual quality.

source.caption:
Figure 1: Motivation of UCMIT. Unlike position-wise fusion under cross-modal misalignment,
UCMIT retrieves complementary thermal evidence from plausible nearby locations and reconstructs
it in RGB coordinates before representation update.

observations.evidence: The crossed-out position-wise fusion contrasts clearly with transport producing RGB-aligned thermal evidence. Offset blue and pink cells make the spatial mismatch visible.
observations.limitation: The internal transport diagram does not clearly explain how candidate sources contribute to the aligned output.

source.caption:
Figure 2: Conflicting target assignment in any-depth detectors. (a) In AnyDepth-DETR, the Hungarian
matcher can assign different queries to the same ground-truth objects across the two execution paths.
We reorder the super-net’s foreground queries to align with the base-net’s target-matched query
ordering before applying KD. (b) In AnyDepth-YOLO, the Task-Aligned Assigner (TAL) can assign
the super-net and base-net outputs to different anchors for the same ground-truth object. We exclude
conflicting anchor assignments (in red boxes) from the foreground distillation set.

during the class combination, we identify the potential old classes through the old model. In the instance selection, we select the instances

new image to create a fused image. Finally, the fused image is trained in an enhanced way.

Figure 2: Evidence-grounded agent-as-judge evaluation framework. Given the user request, reference
assets, execution trace, intermediate artifacts, and final video, the evaluation agent conducts an agentic
evaluation. At each round, it invokes evaluation skills to inspect traces, extract video metadata, sample
key frames, separate audio, run ASR, analyze errors, and understand visual or audio content. The
collected evidence is then used to score process and output metrics and provide textual feedback.

source.title: Fractal Calibration for long-tailed object detection
source.role_reason: 图2及第3节给出FRACAL整体流程，包含检测网络、类别频率与分形空间统计、联合校准及输出。
source.caption:
Figure 2. During imbalanced object detection, the model makes more frequent class detections like hat and less rare class detections like
tiara both of which have strong upper location bias. FRACAL utilises fractal dimension and debiases the logits both in the frequency and
space axes, making fewer hat detections and more tiara detections that are both evenly spread in image space.

source.caption:
Fig.3: Overview of VLOD-TTA. Given an input image and a pool of class
prompts, the text encoder produces embeddings that interact with region proposals
through the vision–language head to compute similarity scores. IPS selects the top-ρ
prompts and averages their scores to obtain per-proposal class scores. IWE then com-
bines per-proposal entropy with IoU-based weights to form the adaptation objective.

source.role_reason: 引言第2页以图1指出现有语义分割数据集分辨率和精细边界标注不足；展示标注问题而非模型普通结果对比。
source.caption:
Figure 1. Comparisons on the resolution and annotation quality between existing semantic segmentation datasets (a) COCO, (b) ADE20K,
(c) EntitySeg and (d) our established dataset MaSS13K. Note that the ‘others’ category, which is highlighted in yellow, in our MaSS13K
actually contains a group of well-segmented objects without specific class names. Please zoom-in for a better view.

source.role_reason: 图2明确为EMGauss整体pipeline，包含已知切片、标准高斯、连续变形、可微渲染和光度监督。
source.caption:
Figure 2. Overview of the pipeline of EMGauss. Given a vol-
ume EM dataset (top), the gray-shaded regions denote the miss-
ing intermediate slices to be interpolated, while the visible regions
represent the available anisotropic training data. We interpret the
low-resolution z -axis as a temporal dimension and employ a de-
formable 2D Gaussian splatting representation to model the ge-
ometric evolution of 2D structures along depth. During inference,
the model synthesizes the target slice by directly conditioning on
the relative temporal coordinate corresponding to the desired in-
terpolation position.

source.caption:
Figure 2: Why over-segmentation defeats confidence-based suppression in the few-shot regime. (a) Real
scenes contain multiple overlapping same-class instances, so class-agnostic proposal generators fragment ob-
jects into nested, mutually overlapping proposals that simple merging cannot consolidate. (b) The smaller
member of a nested pair is occasionally a genuine, distinct object, so the covered box cannot simply be dis-
carded. (c) Few-shot support sets are frequently biased: a handful of examples may emphasise part-views and
fail to represent the class as a whole. (d) Under such bias, the prototype shifts towards part-views, and an
over-segmentation fragment can attain higher classification confidence than the correct whole-object proposal.

source.caption:
Figure 2. An overview of the FaithDiff, which takes LQ images and image descriptions as inputs and restores HQ images via diffusion
process. To fully leverage the power of LDMs, we propose to unleash diffusion priors. An alignment module is developed to effectively
incorporate the features extracted from LQ images with the noisy latent of the diffusion model. We jointly optimize the encoder, the
alignment module, and the diffusion model, which can benefit from their interplay and lead to faithful SR images with high visual quality.

source.caption:
Figure 1: (a) A brief illustration of the current Grounding-DINO-based works. (b) We find that
compared with the ground-truth bounding box (red), for target domains, the top-ranked candidate
boxes (yellow) are less likely to tightly bound the objects, where the better candidate boxes (cyan)
may be ranked outside the Top-900 quota. Unlike current work, we identify the selected candidate
boxes as another bottleneck for the CD-FSOD task, which we aim to address in this paper.

source.caption:
Figure 2. An overview of the proposed RSCN. For every batch, source-domain images with labeled foreground objects and target-domain
images without foreground objects are fed to the detector. The background prototypes are aligned with the BPA objective in Eq. 5. RSH in
Eq. 6 keeps the relative geometric relationship for the source and target background prototypes to the shared foreground prototype anchors.
A frozen reference detector is utilized to maintain the source-domain structure in order to avoid the feature collapse with SSP in Eq. 7.

observations.limitation: SSP, RSH, and BPA are unexplained, and the crossed-eye symbol leaves the target foreground's treatment uncertain.

ID to isolate prompt, which forces task-general prompt to be re-

source.caption:
Figure 3. Overview of DORNet. Given D as input, the degradation learning first encodes it to produce degradation representations D˜
up
and D. Then, D˜, D, D , and I are fed into multiple degradation-oriented feature transformation (DOFT) modules, generating the HR
lr
depth D . Finally, D and D are sent to the degradation regularization to obtain D , which is used as input for the degradation loss
hr hr d
L and the contrastive loss L . The degradation regularization only applies during training and adds no extra overhead in testing.
deg cont

observations.evidence: The lower stream traces depth and image inputs through DOFT blocks to a high-resolution depth output. The upper stream visibly connects degradation learning, routed generators, filtering, and training losses.
observations.limitation: DOFT's function and the precise distinction between training and testing paths remain implicit.

observations.evidence: The upper degradation-learning branch feeds the lower fusion pipeline, whose depth and RGB inputs lead to a high-resolution depth output. The right-hand paths explicitly connect outputs to degradation, contrastive, and reconstruction losses.
observations.limitation: The frozen contrastive module and the two conditioning signals entering DOFT are not clearly identified.

observations.evidence: The lower pipeline visibly combines low-resolution depth and an RGB image through DOFT blocks to produce high-resolution depth. The upper branch connects learned degradation, routed generators, filtering, and training losses.
observations.limitation: The roles of the two curved conditioning inputs to DOFT and the precise relationship between filtering and summation remain unclear.

observations.evidence: Green and peach regions separate degradation learning from fusion, with a predominantly left-to-right flow. The bottom-right legend makes operation symbols readily accessible.
observations.limitation: Generator connections and the tightly packed loss branches require more careful tracing.

observations.evidence: Green and peach regions separate the two main processes, and most computation proceeds left to right. The crops make the component labels and operation legend readable.
observations.limitation: Routing switches, kernel outputs, filtering, and loss connections crowd the right half; curved connections between regions require additional tracing.

observations.evidence: Green and peach bands separate degradation learning from fusion, while headings distinguish the upper submodules. The main computation proceeds left to right, with a readable symbol legend below.
observations.limitation: Generator routing and the loss connections on the right create locally dense regions that require careful tracing.

source.role_reason: 图3明确为整体CUPID流程：占据与姿态生成、PnP相机恢复、姿态对齐条件以及几何外观输出。
source.caption:
Figure 3. Overview of CUPID’s pipeline. From a single input image, CUPID first generates an occupancy and a UV cube in canonical
space. Then, a Perspective-n-Point (PnP) solver (i.e., Eq. 2) recovers the camera pose. Using this recovered camera pose, we extract pose-
aligned conditioning latents and visual features (i.e., Eq. 3), along with noisy structured latents, to generate the geometry and appearance
features, which will be decoded to the 3D Gaussian splats and mesh.

Figure 2: Overview of our proposed VEvo-Harness pipeline. A self-evolving scaffold is built around
(a) a Interaction Loop for generation and verification, comprising (b) Visual Traceback, (c) Visual
Continual Governance, (d) Lifecycle-Managed Harness State, and (e) Heterogeneous Action Sandbox.

source.role_reason: 引言第2页引用图1解释单一class token的类无关注意力及定位歧义；整图对比单token和多token概念，是引出问题的范式对比。
source.caption:
Figure 1. (a) In previous vision transformers [10], only one class
token (red square) is used to aggregate information from patch to-
kens (blue square). The learned patch attentions corresponding
to the class token generate a class-agnostic localization map. (b)
In contrast, the proposed MCTformer uses multiple class tokens
to learn interactions between class tokens and patch tokens. The
learned class-to-patch attentions of different class tokens can pro-
duce class-specific object localization maps.

Figure 1: Motivation for density consensus learning. OPT and SAR observations provide heteroge-
neous and spatially varying evidence for the same underlying ship distribution. We establish their
agreement in a shared density space to preserve mutually supported target responses while suppress-
ing modality-specific interference. Different Gaussian bandwidths in (d) illustrate the dependence
of conventional pixel-wise density targets on predefined kernel shapes.

source.title: LAB-Det: Language as a Domain-Invariant Bridge for Training-Free One-Shot Domain Generalization in Object Detection
source.role_reason: 图2是完整LAB-Det流程，从示例解析、文本构造、冻结检测到分数校准。
source.caption:
Figure 2. Overview of LAB-Det. Top: exemplar-to-language projection. A single annotated exemplar is segmented by SAM and described
by DAM under a domain-aware prompt, yielding natural-language phrases (e.g., “rough texture”). Bottom: these phrases condition a
frozen detector (e.g., Grounding DINO) to generate candidate boxes and phrase scores. Category scores are obtained by averaging phrase
scores, and an optional BLIP-based calibration refines small or ambiguous detections. The entire pipeline is training-free and interpretable.

source.caption:
Figure 2. The pipeline of the PointOBB. PointOBB contains three views in total. From these views, an angle acquisition module and
a scale augmentation module are constructed. The scale augmentation module incorporates a Scale-Sensitive Consistency (SSC) loss to
enhance scale perception ability. Within the angle acquisition module, a Dense-to-Dense sample assignment is designed for angle learning,
optimized using the Self-Supervised Angle (SSA) loss. Additionally, a Dense-to-Sparse (DS) matching strategy is proposed to obtain more
precise object angles. During the training, a progressive multi-view switching strategy is designed to switch the resized and rot/flp views,
along with their corresponding modules.

source.caption:
Figure 3. Flowchart of the proposed single-stage SASS method, which is realized by incorporating an auxiliary branch into the traditional
segmentation model S(·). During training, the predicted masks P are split into the labeled and unlabeled parts, which are supervised by
the segmentation loss L and the tree energy loss L , respectively. To obtain pseudo labels for unlabeled pixels, the Tree Affinity
seg tree
Generation procedure (Eqs. 3-5) first utilizes the color information I and semantic features F to generate the low-level and high-level
affinity matrices Alow,Ahigh. Then the Cascaded Filtering operation (Eqs. 6-7) converts the network predictions P into soft pseudo labels
Y˜. During testing, the auxiliary branch is removed to avoid extra computational costs.

source.role_reason: 引言第2页借图1分析VFM细节强但缺少文本对齐、VLM对齐强但定位粗糙的互补局限；不是仅性能柱状图。保留整图中的定量柱状附图。
source.caption:
Figure 1. Comparative analysis of the VFM and the VLM fea-
tures. VFM: Visualization of PCA-computed features from DI-
NOv2 (the first three components of PCA, computed on the image
features, serve as color channels), displaying fine-grained details
but lacking text alignment. VLM: Image-text similarity map from
EVA02-CLIPusingthequery‘car’,demonstratinggoodalignment
with text but insufficient localization of queried objects. MFuser:
OurproposedfusionframeworkintegratesVFMandVLM,result-
ing in unified features that exhibit both precise locality and robust
text alignment. Quantitative results on synthetic-to-real DGSS
benchmarks further validate our approach, with MFuser consis-
tently achieving the highest mIoU scores across all tasks.

Figure 1. Overview of PanoVGGT and the PanoCity dataset. PanoVGGT predicts camera poses, dense depth, and consistent 3D point
clouds from unordered panoramas. Compared with perspective-based pipelines that split panoramas into pinhole views, it yields more
accurate 3D reconstructions. PanoCity contains over 120k outdoor panoramas under diverse urban scenes and weather conditions.

Figure 2. Approach Overview. We first pre-train a reconstruction model using multi-view renderings of synthetic data. We then self-train
category-specific models on diverse image collections in-the-wild with only foreground mask annotations. We finally distill the learned
models from prior training stages into a unified reconstruction model.

source.caption:
Figure 2. Proposed MoCE-IR framework. Despite recent advances in MoE-based image restoration [57, 62, 63], inconsistent expert
behavior—where some experts over-generalize while others underperform—limits their computational efficiency. We address this through
complexity experts: flexible blocks with varying computational capacity and receptive fields. Our MoCE-IR employs an asymmetric
encoder-decoder architecture where each decoder block contains a mixture-of-complexity-experts layer for adaptive capacity routing.

source.title: Hunting Attributes: Context Prototype-Aware Learning for Weakly Supervised Semantic Segmentation
source.role_reason: 图2(a)是完整分类到分割训练流程，(b)是原型感知学习，全部保留。
source.caption:
Figure 2. Overview of the proposed unified learning framework. (a) shows image label-guided WSSS (from classification to segmentation).
The upper branch describes the classification network θ identifying object regions corresponding to each category to minimize LBC E .
Introduce a self-supervised learning paradigm using context prototype-aware learning to provide a more complete CAM, supervising the
initial CAM and minimizing LS elf . The lower branch refines these CAMs (e.g., DenceCRF [26]) to form pseudo-labels for supervising the
semantic segmentation network. (b) outlines our strategy based on context prototype-aware learning. In mini-batches, instance prototypes
P I are generated using CAM and extracted features f , updating the support bank. Then, the bank is used to construct a context prototype
n
set P c . Feature distribution alignment is then applied to the current instance features, adding a shift term δ to guide them toward clusters of
n n
dense features in the bank. Next, soft neighbors are softly measured for P I based on P c , with P I serving as anchors. Finally, positiveness
n n n
value w can be computed between two specific attributes. This mechanism selects K soft positive neighbors P˜ c to generate PACAM.
i n

source.title: GDPO-SR: Group Direct Preference Optimization for One-Step Generative Image Super-Resolution
source.role_reason: 第3节及图2完整展示参考模型生成样本、奖励优势计算、策略模型优化两阶段训练框架。
source.caption:
Figure 2. The framework of GDPO, which consists of two core stages: (a) advantage calculation and (b) policy optimization. Firstly, we
employ a pre-trained one-step Real-ISR model as the reference model to generate a group of diverse outputs by injecting different random
noises. Subsequently, we compute the advantage A for each sample by evaluating its reward with our designed attribute-aware reward
functions and converting these rewards into group-relative advantages. In the policy optimization stage, we feed these samples along with
noises into both the policy model and the reference ISR model, and update the parameters of the policy ISR model by minimizing the
proposed GDPO loss, steering it to favor generating high-reward samples.

source.role_reason: 图1以训练类别及昼夜/雾天域变化和部署未知类别解释演化世界检测的问题设置，属于应用场景与任务动机。
source.caption:
Figure 1. Overview of Evolving World Object Detection (EWOD). Top (Training): Sequential tasks introduce disjoint classes K across
t
shifting domains D (Day → Night → Fog). Bottom (Deployment): The detector must (i) identify unseen objects U without supervision;
t t
(ii) retain knowledge of all prior classes across all domains; (iii) incrementally learn former unknowns when their labels are revealed later
(e.g., U → K ) and (iv) achieve all these objectives without revisiting any previous data. Best viewed in colour with zoom1 .
2 3

source.role_reason: 引言图1以盆栽误识别为鸟的案例解释低熵、高置信度和不一致性三种标注策略的失败机制。
source.caption:
Figure 1. An object from a low-performing class (Pottedplant),
original image in blue, augmented version in orange. a) Because
of its low-entropy, uncertainty-based AL methods do not label the
image. b) Because of its high confidence, pseudo-label SSL meth-
ods wrongly pseudo-label the image and thus harm the training. c)
Because of its high-inconsistency, consistency-based SSL meth-
ods cannot learn from it. d) Our method selects the image for
labeling and prevents it from getting pseudo-labeled.

source.title: Adversarial Diffusion Compression for Real-World Image Super-Resolution
source.role_reason: 第3.3节及图3展示两阶段训练与推理、教师学生判别器及各损失的完整流程。
source.caption:
Figure3. IllustrationofthetrainingandinferenceprocessesofAdcSR,aninstantiationofourADCframeworkappliedtoOSEDiff.
(a)InStage1,wepretrainaprunedVAEdecoderthatsharesthelatentspacewithSDandOSEDiff. (b)InStage2,wedistilltheknowledge
from OSEDiff (ADC-teacher) into AdcSR (ADC-student) by aligning features in the pretrained decoder. An adversarial loss encourages
the student to generate features that can fool a LoRA-finetuned SD UNet (ADC-discriminator), utilizing the corresponding real features
of GT images. Since all supervisions perform in the feature space, there is no need to decode images as in previous approaches [96, 112].
(c) During inference, the LR image is directly fed into our trained compressed UNet and VAE decoder to obtain the super-resolution result.

trained/finetuned on different datasets. FoundIR shows limited generalization to real rain and haze,
even after finetuned on existing restoration datasets. Qwen-Image-Edit produces sharper details with

datasets weakens its detail generation ability. GGT-100K significantly improves the generalization
capability of them to real-world degradations, enhancing visual details while preserving scene fidelity.

Figure 2: Pipeline of Sprout. Three questions about one video are answered in order, building one
memory. Each row shows the rounds of one question: tool calls (circles) and their results (boxes).
Video frames stay in the context for one round only; text results are kept. Q1 watches the first two
chunks, remembers them as coarse nodes, and revisits n at a higher frame rate to add finer child
2
nodes. Q2 reuses the memory: search returns a node and Q1’s answer, and a short revisit adds one
more detail, without watching new video. Q3 finds that the memory does not cover what it asks, so
it watches two more chunks. The last two chunks are never watched. The memory tree (bottom) is
drawn on the same time axis as the video; node colors show which question added each node.

Figure 3: Overview of UniForge3D. Left: The reconstruction and generation branches interact
bidirectionally to predict multi-view point maps and a complete sparse structure in a shared anchor-
guided space. Right: Structure-conditioned point maps establish voxel-to-pixel correspondences,
enabling the model to select informative views and use their image features to guide detailed shape
generation.

combined with text prompts to create the dual-prompt cost volume. Subsequently, we incorporate multi-scale image features and corre-
sponding visual prompt embeddings into the cost volume-guided decoder (CVGD) in a progressive manner.

Figure 2. Pipeline of DW. The left part shows the overall detection model which consists of backbone, FPN and detection head. The
outputs from the classification branch (H × W × C) and the centerness branch (H × W × 1) are multiplied as the final cls score. The
box refinement module utilizes the four predicted boundary points (H × W × 8) to adjust the coarse prediction (H × W × 4) to finer
locations.The right part shows the weighting process. Given an object, a candidate anchor bag is first constructed by selecting the anchor
points near the object center. Each anchor will then be assigned a pos weight and neg weight from different aspects.

source.caption:
Fig.1: Motivation for IWE. Left→right: (i) Raw predictions before thresholding
for two classes — a true positive Person (red) (bbox cluster size = 167, max score
= 0.14) and a false positive Dog (blue) (bbox cluster size = 45, max score = 0.15);
(ii) In ZS, all scores remain below the detection threshold, causing a missed detection;
(iii) Standard entropy minimization over-confidently sharpens scores, resulting in a dog
false positive; and (iv) IWE focuses updates on dense bbox clusters and suppresses
isolated boxes, producing only the correct person detection.

source.caption:
Figure 1. We present G²VLM, a geometry grounded vision-language model proficient in both spatial 3D reconstruction and spatial
understanding tasks. For spatial reasoning questions, G²VLM can predict 3D geometry and employ interleaved reasoning for an answer.

source.caption:
Figure 1: Two sources of mismatch when using pretrained image priors in scientific imaging:
differences between the pretraining and target image domains, and differences between score-model
training inputs and ADMM denoiser inputs.

observations.evidence: Two labeled comparisons explicitly distinguish domain mismatch from solver-input mismatch. The adjacent iterative diagram shows where the pretrained diffusion prior enters PnP-ADMM.

weighted subproblems. Each subproblem keeps a harness and together they approximate the Pareto
frontier. (b) An LLM proposer diagnoses failures and forms a hypothesis. Operators edit tools, skills,
or logic, and place each edit in either the general scope or the environment-specific scope. The child
is validated before evaluation. (c) At inference, a composition agent picks components from the
general and environment-specific pools to build a task-specific harness.

Figure 3: Overview of AKI. (a) Three-level knowledge reorganization. (b) RCA constructs compact
response support and enforces response consistency. (c) RPA discovers reusable semantic directions
for selective alignment. (d) DEP suppresses current old–new distribution overlap.

source.title: CrossSDF: 3D Reconstruction of Thin Structures From Cross-Sections
source.role_reason: 图2及3.1节明确为完整pipeline，含截面输入、自适应采样、混合编码、SDF网络、损失及三维输出。
source.caption:
Figure 2. CrossSDF takes a set of planar cross-sections as input. These cross-sections result in contours which denote the surface
boundaries of the target geometry of interest (left, black lines) and each induces a 2D signed distance field (SDF) in its respective plane.
From this, we generate a set of planar sample points Ω and their 2D SDF labels. During training, points are encoded using our hybrid
pl
encoder before being passed to the SDF network M for prediction. At each iteration we create a set of 3D samples Ω to apply
SDF reg
volumetric regularization. The combination of our novel sampling, loss function, and hybrid encoding results in a high quality 3D SDF.

source.role_reason: 图注明确称SED整体框架，包含教师学生、尺度一致性、自蒸馏、重加权和EMA；保留图内用于解释流程的失败示例。
source.caption:
Figure 1. The overall framework of SED. Our model improves the
scale equivalence, which is critical for object detectors, by regu-
larizing the consistency between different-sized images. Further-
more, the inherent False Negative sample noise is alleviated by
self-distillation. A re-weighting strategy is adopted to solve the
severe class imbalance problem. The bird in the left example is a
False Negative sample when the threshold is set to 0.7. The right
example shows the scale inconsistency of different-sized images.

adaptive market, delayed-payoff investments).

source.title: Multi-Class Token Transformer for Weakly Supervised Semantic Segmentation
source.role_reason: 第3.1节Overview明确称图2为MCTformer-V1整体架构；包含输入token化、多层编码、分类及注意力细化完整路径。
source.caption:
Figure 2. An overview of the proposed multi-class token transformer (MCTformer-V1). It first splits and transforms an input RGB image
into a sequence of patch tokens. We propose to learn C extra class tokens, where C is the number of classes. The C class tokens are
concatenated with patch tokens, with added position embeddings (PE), which then go through consecutive L transformer encoding layers.
Finally, the output C class tokens are used to produce class scores via average pooling. We aggregate the transformer attentions from the
last K layers and multiple heads to generate a final attention map, from which we can extract class-specific object localization maps and a
patch-level pairwise affinity map from the class-to-patch and the patch-to-patch attentions, respectively. The patch-level pairwise affinity
can be used to refine the class-specific transformer attention maps to produce improved object localization maps.

source.caption:
Figure 2. Overview of the proposed PanoVGGT framework. Given one or multiple panoramic images, PanoVGGT extracts spherical
patch tokens using a ViT backbone, augments them via S O(3) geometric augmentation, and encodes them with shared and branch-adapted
positional embeddings. A multi-branch attention aggregator jointly reasons about local geometry, global structure, and camera motion.
The model outputs dense depth maps, camera poses (under a randomly selected global anchor), and local/global point maps for final 3D
reconstruction.

observations.evidence: The main sequence connects panoramic inputs, ViT features, positional embeddings, an attention aggregator, and three prediction branches. Depth maps, cameras, and a reconstructed scene make the output setting concrete.
observations.limitation: The augmentation panel’s connection to the main process and the branch-specific paths to outputs remain unclear.

observations.evidence: Panoramas feed a ViT, token processing, an attention aggregator, and three labeled prediction branches, followed by reconstruction outputs.
observations.limitation: The connections between branch-specific positional encoding, individual outputs, and the random reference frame remain unclear.

observations.evidence: Panoramas feed a ViT, token processing, an attention aggregator, and three labeled prediction branches. Depth maps, cameras, and a reconstructed scene establish the intended outputs.
observations.limitation: The connections between branch-adapted positional encoding, prediction branches, and the random reference anchor remain unclear.

observations.evidence: Bounded panels separate augmentation, spherical embedding, attention, and outputs around a broadly left-to-right pipeline. The crops make the main component labels readable.
observations.limitation: Supporting modules above and below the pipeline compete for attention, while crowded junctions and pale connectors make some transitions difficult to follow.

observations.evidence: Enclosed regions separate augmentation, spherical embedding, attention, prediction branches, and outputs. The main architecture broadly reads left to right.
observations.limitation: Dense legends, vertical labels, and auxiliary modules above and below the pipeline make the complete reading sequence effortful.

observations.evidence: The main pipeline runs left to right, with positional embedding above and branch adaptation below. Bordered panels separate the augmentation examples and output visualizations.
observations.limitation: Dense auxiliary panels and large pale connectors make the reading sequence around the central pipeline require extra effort.

observations.evidence: Repeated token colors and legends distinguish patch tokens, positional embeddings, and their combined representation. Blue, orange, and purple consistently identify the three branches in both central and lower panels.
observations.limitation: The branch colors are not carried clearly into the output panel, and broad pale connectors obscure the correspondence between branches and results.

observations.evidence: Blue, orange, and purple consistently distinguish the three branches and their positional-encoding modules; token colors recur through attention.
observations.limitation: Pale broad arrows, thin dashed lines, and small directional arrows express relationships with uneven precision, especially around the branches and outputs.

observations.evidence: Repeated token colors connect the input token stacks to the attention blocks. Blue, orange, and purple consistently distinguish the three branches across two regions.
observations.limitation: The broad pale connectors do not make individual branch-to-output relationships consistently traceable.

observations.evidence: Pastel panel backgrounds and repeated rounded containers provide a coherent overall structure. Large scene examples balance the central schematic.
observations.limitation: Serif, sans-serif, italic, and handwritten text compete alongside shadows, reflective effects, and varied border treatments.

observations.evidence: Pastel panel backgrounds and repeated rounded containers provide a shared visual structure.
observations.limitation: The handwritten cloud, bold serif headings, italic titles, shadows, and varied icons compete for emphasis in an already dense composition.

observations.evidence: Pastel panel backgrounds and coordinated branch colors provide visual cohesion. The reconstruction gives the output region a clear visual focus.
observations.limitation: Mixed serif, sans-serif, italic, and handwritten text, together with shadows and the cloud callout, create competing styles and uneven emphasis.

observations.evidence: The panorama wrapped onto a sphere and the rotated panorama examples explain the spherical geometry visually. The reference-image scene arrangement and coordinate axes give the world-frame concept a concrete spatial representation.
observations.limitation: These explanatory devices are only partly integrated into the main computational flow.

observations.evidence: The textured sphere with coordinate axes and angular embedding planes makes spherical positioning tangible. Rotated panorama examples illustrate the augmentation operation.
observations.limitation: The random-anchor illustration establishes a spatial setting but only loosely explains how that frame relates to the computational pipeline.

observations.evidence: A panorama wrapped onto a coordinate sphere explains the spatial basis of positional embedding. Rotated panorama examples and camera markers around the reconstruction make the geometric task concrete.
observations.limitation: The rainbow embedding tiles and repeated branch modules convey less about the actual transformation than the geometric illustrations do.

observations.evidence: Spherical panorama projection, azimuth and polar coordinates, SO3 rotation examples, and distinct global/local point branches visibly tailor the architecture to panoramic reconstruction. Camera markers and depth maps connect its outputs to the illustrated scene.
observations.limitation: The branch-adapted encoding diagrams show little about how the three adaptations differ beyond their labels and colors.

observations.evidence: Panorama rotation examples, spherical coordinates, global/local point branches, and camera-linked room reconstruction express distinctive operations and outputs of this framework.
observations.limitation: The attention and branch-adapter internals use generic token stacks and module silhouettes.

observations.evidence: Spherical coordinates, rotated panoramic views, a reference-defined world frame, and camera-linked point maps visibly express distinctive parts of panoramic reconstruction.
observations.limitation: The attention aggregator itself uses broadly reusable token-stack notation.
